1. **`package.json` — grammar-test skip branch silently swallows `test-grammar` failures.** `([ $# -eq 0 ] && npm run test-grammar || echo "Skipping...")` is parsed as `(A && B) || C`. If no filter is given (A true) and `npm run test-grammar` (B) fails, the `&&` pair fails, so `C` (the `echo`) runs and its exit code (0) becomes the exit code of the whole expression — a real grammar-test failure is masked as success. Fix: use an explicit `if`, e.g. `if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then npm run test-grammar; else echo "Skipping grammar tests when filter provided"; fi`, and make sure the `if` block's own exit status propagates.

2. **`package.json` — `sh -c '...' --` breaks on Windows, which the linked issue explicitly requires to keep working.** Native Windows npm installs run scripts via `cmd.exe`, where `sh` is not available by default (no `$@` argv-forwarding semantics, no `&&`/`||` short-circuit guarantees the same way). This needs a cross-platform solution (e.g. a small Node/JS helper script invoked from `test`/`test-only`, or `cross-env`-style tooling) rather than inline POSIX shell, and should be verified on an actual Windows/cmd.exe run, not just assumed.

3. **`src/test/test_runner.ts` — multi-word filters don't actually work as claimed.** `test_all.ts` joins all CLI args with a space (`testFilterArgs.join(" ")`) and `test_runner.ts` drops that joined string whole into `**/*${testFilter}*.test.js`. Since file paths never contain spaces, any multi-argument filter (e.g. `npm test go to`) will match zero files — contradicting the PR description's claim that "multiple word filters" are supported. Each arg should be treated as an independent substring filter (OR'd or AND'd explicitly), not concatenated into one literal glob segment.

4. **`src/test/test_runner.ts` — unescaped user input interpolated into a glob pattern.** `` `**/*${testFilter}*.test.js` `` passes the raw filter straight into `glob()`. Filter strings containing glob metacharacters (`*`, `?`, `[`, `]`, `(`, `)`, etc. — plausible given real test file names/describe blocks) will produce an unintended or invalid pattern. Escape glob-special characters in `testFilter` before interpolating.

5. **`src/test/test_runner.ts` — early `resolve()` on no-match skips Mocha entirely, including reporter setup.** When `files.length === 0`, the function returns before `mocha.run()` is ever invoked, so the configured `MultiReporter` (which writes `TEST_XML_OUTPUT`) never produces its output file. Any CI step that expects that XML/report file to exist (even for a no-op run) will fail downstream. Either still invoke the reporter with zero files, or document/guard the missing-file case in whatever consumes `TEST_XML_OUTPUT`.

6. **`package.json` — `npm run test-only "$@"` inside the outer `test` script omits `--` before forwarding.** If a future filter argument looks like a flag (e.g. `npm test -- --something`), npm itself may try to interpret it rather than passing it through to the `test-only` script. Use `npm run test-only -- "$@"` for unambiguous argument forwarding.
